summary: Puerto Rico is a tight economic engine-builder where you balance producing goods, shipping them before the boats fill up, and building an efficient production chain with limited colonists. Every role you pick benefits all players, so the real skill is choosing roles that help you more than your opponents.
praised: Deep, elegant economic engine with almost no luck
Role-selection mechanism where every choice benefits everyone but you get the edge
High replayability from different building/strategy combinations
Strong sense of engine optimization and satisfying long-term planning
criticised: Can feel solitaire-ish with limited direct interaction beyond shipping and role choice
Downtime between turns, especially at higher player counts
Corn/theme is thin and abstract despite the colonial setting
Colonization theme has drawn criticism as dated/uncomfortable for some players

interaction.kind: role selection denial and competition for shared shipping space

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Victory points come almost entirely from buildings and shipped goods, so the winner is decided by production efficiency and building point value, not diverse scoring categories
